courses.name: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Procedural and object-oriented programming through exercises using types, control flow, collections and custom objects.

courses.name: Mathematics for Computer Science
courses.description: Discrete mathematics, proof techniques, graphs, counting and asymptotic analysis with Python assignments.

courses.name: Data Structures
courses.description: Implement and analyze fundamental data structures, emphasizing efficient and reliable programs.

courses.name: Computer Organization
courses.description: C and assembly programming, memory management, processor architecture and program optimization.

courses.name: Algorithms
courses.description: Design, implement and compare algorithms using empirical and formal complexity analysis.

courses.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: Algorithm design and analysis, including computability, complexity, design strategies and correctness.

courses.name: Modern Data Management
courses.description: Build streaming and batch pipelines to integrate and transform enterprise data across different storage systems.

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.description: Operating-system design covering processes, concurrency, memory, storage, files and security.

courses.name: Programming Languages
courses.description: Programming-language concepts, syntax, semantics and implementation explored through coding in multiple languages.
courses.prerequisites: COM 2545 may be taken as a prerequisite or corequisite.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: AI foundations and methods, including reasoning, planning, representation and learning, with programming and writing assignments.

courses.name: Distributed Systems
courses.description: Challenges and techniques for scalable, available distributed services, including cloud computing.

courses.name: Parallel Algorithms and Programming
courses.description: Parallel-system tradeoffs, concurrent programming and parallel algorithm design.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Machine-learning principles, algorithms, applications and industry libraries for prediction from data.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Analyze text computationally to extract meaning for applications such as sentiment analysis and information retrieval.

courses.name: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Build and deploy practical machine-learning applications and production systems.
courses.prerequisites: COM 3760 and COM 3920 ; and COM 3800 may be taken as a prerequisite or corequisite.

courses.name: Capstone Project
courses.description: Faculty-supervised software engineering project meeting functional and technical requirements. Collaboration across tracks requires faculty approval.

courses.name: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, differentiation and applications, followed by fundamental integration methods.
courses.prerequisites: Online placement test given before the semester.

courses.name: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration techniques and applications, series, parametric curves and polar coordinates.

courses.name: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Multivariable and vector calculus, including constrained optimization and integral theorems.

courses.name: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Linear systems, matrices, vector spaces, transformations, eigenstructure and applications.

courses.name: Probability Theory
courses.description: Probability models, random variables, expectation, limit theorems and random walks; described as semi-online.

courses.name: Mathematical Statistics
courses.description: Statistical estimation, inference, regression and categorical data; assumes calculus, linear algebra and probability knowledge.

requirements.title: AI concentration required courses
requirements.summary: Complete the published AI concentration course table (75 source-stated credits). This includes common CS and mathematics requirements of the host major.

requirements.title: Major grades and progression
requirements.summary: Yeshiva College requires a major GPA of at least 2.000, at least C- in every course counted toward the major, and at least C- in prerequisites to advance. The university also requires an overall GPA of 2.000; this is context, not a complete degree audit.

requirements.title: Major residence and individual transfer review
requirements.summary: At least 60% of the major/minor must be completed in residence for the standard entry route and, generally, for transfer students. Transfer students must consult an adviser about their applicable residency requirements. Additional degree-wide residence rules depend on entry history; no single degree-wide credit threshold is assigned to this concentration.

requirements.title: Major declaration and catalog applicability
requirements.summary: Declare a major through the Registrar by 60 earned credits, including transferred credits; undeclared students may receive a registration hold. Use the Declaration of Academic Major and Minors form. A change follows the catalog of the change year, may be filed once per registration period without adviser approval, and cannot follow a graduation application. A separate AI concentration declaration procedure is not established by this general policy.

requirements.title: Letter grades for required courses
requirements.summary: For Yeshiva College on the Wilf Campus, P grades cannot satisfy major/minor requirements or required major correlates. P/N is limited to free electives for students beyond freshman year in good standing; it does not replace the required concentration course grades.

requirements.title: Written substitution approval
requirements.summary: An academic adviser may authorize a substitute course in writing after approval from the department chair or dean’s office. A substitution is an individual decision, not an additional published concentration option.

requirements.title: Prior approval for outside coursework
requirements.summary: Obtain school approval and the appropriate outside-course request form before enrollment, normally only in summer. Supply a syllabus unless the course is pre-approved. Community-college and unaccredited courses are not approved. Approved courses need at least C; grades do not enter the YU GPA. Summer courses last at least four weeks. Session credit caps are 4/7/8/9/10 for sessions lasting 4/5/6/7/8 weeks, with at most 10 credits across the summer. Quarter conversion is 4 credits to 2.5 YU credits or 5 to 3. Department-specific CS/math summer approval still applies.

requirements.title: Transfer evaluation is individual
requirements.summary: After admission, prior courses require an official transcript and a full syllabus for evaluation. YU normally accepts aligned courses from regionally accredited institutions with at least C; acceptance is individually determined. Current students need prior adviser approval. High-school college coursework has a separate bachelor’s limit of nine credits and B- minimum, requires official transcripts during admission and syllabi, and does not meet residence requirements. Experiential-learning transfer credit is not awarded to students admitted from Fall 2024.

requirements.title: Prerequisite and corequisite compliance
requirements.summary: A prerequisite precedes the dependent course; a corequisite is taken concurrently, and a concurrent prerequisite permits either timing. Students earning below C- in a prerequisite may be removed from the subsequent course. Individual requisites must be checked in the course description in Self Service.

requirements.title: Course overlap requires department policy
requirements.summary: Ordinarily one course may count between general education and a major/minor. Credit-intensive programs may permit more under their department’s policy. Departments also set sharing rules between majors/minors. This general rule is not a numerical cap on the AI track’s published math-minor overlap.

requirements.title: Summer Classes
requirements.summary: CS summer courses require prior written permission from the CS department chair; they are not normally permitted. Required MAT courses taken in summer need approval of the specific course and institution by the math department.

requirements.title: A.P. in C.S. Exemption
requirements.summary: The CS department does not exempt COM 1300 based on the AP Computer Science exam.

requirements.title: A.I. track and Math Minor
requirements.summary: The department states that completing the BS in CS AI track also earns the mathematics minor without additional classes. This is a published overlap, not a separate complete mathematics-minor audit.

notes: The catalog explicitly names a concentration; the department guide calls it a track. This is not a standalone AI degree and is not assigned to Stern College’s separate CS BA.

The registrar identifies the rolling catalog as 2026–27. Individual course pages independently match all 22 required-table codes, titles and credits. Course credits and the 75-credit table total use semester units under the currently linked institutional credit-hour definition, dated November 1, 2018; this is not a calendar-based assumption or a reconciliation with the guide’s 74-credit summary.

The Spring 2026 guide’s comparison table states 74 AI-track credits, while its detailed plan and current catalog state 75; the current catalog’s 22 rows sum to 75. Discrepancy retained, not silently reconciled.

Partial local inventory: the current published major grades, residence, declaration, letter-grade, transfer, substitution, prerequisite and sharing policies plus three CS-specific FAQ rules are reviewed. They preserve individual approval and transfer-history qualifications. General education and the full host BS are not inventoried or certified; no separate AI-track declaration/certification process was found in these reviewed sources. The guide/catalog credit conflict remains unresolved.

The finite 22-course-page queue is reviewed: 22 original description summaries, 21 source-stated prerequisite/corequisite strings, and one unstated prerequisite field (COM 1300) retained as null. COM 3640/4010 prerequisite-or-corequisite alternatives, COM 3800 corequisite and COM 4020 prerequisite alternatives remain explicit. Prerequisite presence does not establish course availability or individual eligibility.

Institutional decisions remain for transfer acceptance, substitutions, CS summer permission and individual residence determinations. All 22 current linked course pages and the credit-policy immediate link chain were inspected successfully. Section-specific teaching sites/syllabi and launch-date or assessed-outcome research remain outside this bounded pass; they are not declared unavailable.

Course source_id now identifies its exact catalog course page; the requirement node still cites the AI concentration table. The separately registered credit-hour-definition source supports semester normalization for every course and the total. Raw course-page parsers leave units unknown; applying the reviewed PDF definition is a separate curated step, and PDF refresh requires a permitted retrieval/extraction and visual review.
